result.notes:
APP-WIDE OUTAGE OBSERVED MID-LANE - NEW F20-9 (critical, two halves). While I was on the resources tab the whole deployment went down for ~2.5 minutes, affecting every lane.

(a) THE DEATH IS SILENT. The app process disappeared at 2026-08-14T17:16:33Z with ZERO diagnostic output: `docker logs -t viberr-app-1` goes straight from "GET /projects/viberr/tasks/VIB-2.data 200 ... 17:16:32.620" to the first restart's refusal at 17:16:33.892 - no stack trace, no FATAL line, no signal note. The app's own fatal channel has the same weakness: app/server/db/data-root-lock.server.ts:466-481 calls logger.error(...) (logger.server.ts:82 = an async process.stdout.write to a pipe) and then process.exit(1) on the next line, which truncates that write.

(b) THE RESTART CANNOT BOOT - self-lockout. Eight consecutive boots printed "Refusing to boot: another Viberr process is already writing /data. Held by pid 1 on host viberr since 2026-08-14T16:50:03.813Z." That is the container refusing to boot on its OWN predecessor's lock: the app runs as pid 1 (/proc/1/cmdline = node /app/node_modules/@react-router/serve/bin.cjs) and compose pins the hostname, so classifyLock (app/server/db/data-root-lock.server.ts:245-252) takes the `holder.hostname === self.hostname` branch and asks isAlive(1) - which in the restarted container is the asking process itself -> verdict "held" -> refuse, forever. The bootId discriminator only rescues the same-process HMR case. Any crash that leaves writer.lock behind therefore bricks the deployment until a human deletes the file. Live sequence (audit_events projection.rescan = one per boot): boot 16:50:03, dead 17:16:33, 8 refusals, boot 17:18:19, dead again by ~17:18:5x, boot 17:18:59 (running since; RestartCount=11, stable for the last ~15 min).

(c) NOT MY MCP SAVE. My credentialed save was in flight at 17:16:33 (its row never reached the DB - no org.mcp.added audit event, no row), but the SECOND death at ~17:18:5x happened with no MCP activity at all, while VIB-3 operator runs and stage transitions fired (audit: runtime.run.started 17:18:39 and 17:18:52, task.transition 17:18:35 and 17:18:49; run_V186s8HmiETU.jsonl's last line at 17:16:32.234Z is the operator selecting mcp__viberr__transition_stage one second before death #1). Both deaths cluster on operator-run/transition activity on VIB-3, another lane's surface.

(d) A PROVEN CANDIDATE MECHANISM for a silent exit-1: an unhandled EPIPE on a piped child's stdin. discoverStdioMcpTools' `send()` (app/server/org/resources.server.ts:911-917) only try/catches SYNCHRONOUSLY and no 'error' listener is ever attached to child.stdin, so a broken-pipe write surfaces as an uncaught exception, which is fatal to the server process. Reproduced inside viberr-app-1 itself: `docker exec viberr-app-1 node /tmp/epipe-probe.js` printed "UNCAUGHT: EPIPE write EPIPE" on 5 of 40 iterations (fast-exiting child + continued stdin writes); the single-write-only variant was clean 120/120, so the exposure is any path that writes to a spawned process's stdin after it may have exited - which includes the run pipeline's CLI children, not just this probe. Repro scripts saved at /Users/akinozer/projects/viberr/.claude/worktrees/viberr-app-inspection-34388a/planning/discovery-2026-08-14-pass20/repro/epipe-probe.js and .../repro/epipe-probe2.js.

Owner follow-up suggestions: (1) attach an 'error' handler wherever the app writes to a child's stdin; (2) add a process-level uncaughtException/unhandledRejection logger that flushes synchronously (fs.writeSync(2, ...)) before exiting so a death is never silent; (3) make classifyLock refuse to treat "pid 1 on my own hostname" as proof of a live predecessor (compare /proc/1 start time, or auto-reclaim when the holder pid equals this process's own pid), so a crash cannot brick the container.

SURFACE HYGIENE: everything I created is gone - org_mcp_servers is back to exactly [everything (up=1), web-fetch (up=0)]. The only residue is web-fetch's last_checked_at moving to my retest (same verdict, same stored error). I never touched the skills card, VIB-1/VIB-2, other lanes' surfaces, the container, compose files, or any repo file.
